title: Insight 1: Nov 1 ride breached easy ceiling by ~8 bpm
description: Your Nov 1 ride averaged 158 bpm, just 1 beat below your Z2 ceiling (159 bpm), and normalized power was 185 W (87% of FTP). For a joyful easy ride, aim to keep avg HR under 145 bpm (mid-Z2) and NP below 160 W.

title: Insight 2: Nov 12 long ride vertical load is high for flat-rolling terrain
description: The Nov 12 ride packed 506 m of climbing into 50 km (10 m/km), the steepest density in your recent block. That's a solid strength stimulus, but pair it with a flatter recovery spin next time to keep legs fresh.

title: Insight 3: Four rides in seven days flags recovery sequencing risk
description: You rode Nov 8, 10, 12, and 14 — four rides in a week with only one rest day. Sleep dipped to 4h42m on Nov 10 and readiness fell to 67 on Nov 12. Consider inserting a full rest day or easy walk after two consecutive ride days.

title: Insight 4: Cycling progression — VO2max steady at 50, FTP likely higher than 213 W
description: Your cycling VO2max has held at 49–50 since late October, but your best 20‑min power jumped to 224 W on Nov 12 (95% = 213 W FTP). That 224 W effort suggests true FTP may be 215–220 W. Celebrate the gain, but don't chase numbers — just enjoy the stronger legs.

title: Insight 5: Zone model check — HR and power zones align reasonably, but FTP may need updating
description: Your HR Z2 (139–159 bpm) and power Z2 (117–160 W) match well on rides like Nov 10 (avg 135 bpm, 136 W). However, FTP 213 W is based on a single 20‑min effort; a fresh 20‑min test or a hard group ride would confirm if zones should shift up.

title: Insight 6: Polarized 80/20 — most rides sit in tempo (Z2), not easy (Z1)
description: Six of your last seven rides averaged 140–158 bpm (Z2), with only Nov 10 at 135 bpm (Z1). For a happier, less fatiguing week, try making 3 of 4 rides truly easy (HR <139 bpm) and save one ride for focused harder efforts.

title: Insight 7: Recovery warning — sleep debt and HRV dip mid‑week
description: Sleep dropped below 5 h on Nov 8, 10, and 12; HRV fell to 57 on Nov 11 and readiness hit 67 on Nov 12. Your body is absorbing the ride load, but the trend says prioritize 7+ h sleep for the next 3 days before adding intensity.

title: Insight 8: Strength — maximal sprint power varies wildly (279–981 W)
description: Your 10‑sec peak power ranges from 279 W (Nov 10) to 981 W (Nov 5), suggesting occasional all‑out sprints but no consistent neuromuscular stimulus. Add 2× 6‑sec seated sprints every 7–10 days on a flat road to build reactive strength without fatigue.

title: Insight 9: VO2max booster — try 4×4 min at 230–240 W with 4 min easy
description: To nudge VO2max above 50, do one weekly session: warm up 20 min, then 4×4 min at 110–115% FTP (≈230–240 W) with 4 min easy spin between. Keep it fun — pick a scenic loop and imagine you're chasing a sunset.

title: Insight 10: FTP suggestion — retest or use 95% of best 20‑min (224 W = 213 W)
description: Your current FTP 213 W comes from 95% of the 224 W 20‑min effort on Nov 12. Garmin's old 271 W is stale. Either do a dedicated 20‑min test on a fresh day, or simply ride hard for 20 min on a quiet road and take 95% of that average — no pressure, just curiosity.
